parts:
We ran into a similar issue (code:127) in our cluster.

After debugging the issue, it was related to missing libR.so in LD_LIBRARY_PATH and the forked task jvms 
(which need -Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib to be passed)

This was fixed like so:

1) Add  
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
 a) to hadoop user's shell env.
 b) to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/hadoop-env.sh
 export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH


2) Add to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/mapred-site.xml

<property>
 <name>mapred.child.jvm.opts</name>
 <value>-Xmx1g -Xms1g  -Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib </value>
</property>


Let me know if this works in your environment,
thanks,
Sri

On Dec 15, 3:07 pm, SriSatish Ambati <srisatish.amb...@gmail.com>

> We ran into a similar issue (code:127) in our cluster.
>
> After debugging the issue, it was related to missing libR.so in
> LD_LIBRARY_PATH and the forked task jvms
> (which need -Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib to be passed)
>
> This was fixed like so:
>
> 1) Add
>   export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
>  a) to hadoop user's shell env.
>  b) to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/hadoop-env.sh
>  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
>
> 2) Add to $HADOOP_HOME/conf/mapred-site.xml
>
> <property>
>  <name>mapred.child.jvm.opts</name>
>  <value>-Xmx1g -Xms1g  *-Djava.library.path=/usr/local/lib64/R/lib* </value>

> </property>
>
> Let me know if this works in your environment,
> thanks,
> Sri

For what it's worth, I've been running on 0.2.203. On a small cluster
where I installed and configured everything myself, I could only make
it work if I was logged in as the hadoop user. On our institutional
cluster, however, I've been running it with no problems. (As an
aside, I'm really curious about how it will work on the nextgen
mapreduce 0.23 stuff from HortonWorks - have you played with this,
Saptarshi?)

The error code 127 has been a linking issue for me, as Sri mentioned.
You may be aware of this trick, but what has helped me figure these
out is the following:

Make a shell script that is executed by the the runner set in
rhoptions to help you diagnose the problem, called, for example
Rsetup.sh:

#!/bin/bash
ldd _path_to_imperious.so_ > ~/lddoutput
exec R CMD _path_to_imperious.so_ --slave --silent --vanilla --max-
ppsize=100000 --max-nsize=1G

Then set it in R before running your Rhipe job with:

rhoptions(runner="_path_to_Rsetup.sh_")

Now when you run a simple job, it will output the ldd output to the
file ~/lddoutput, which you can then inspect to see if there failures
to link. If you are paranoid about environment variables being set
correctly on each node, you can also add those in to the Rsetup.sh
script as well, which might be overkill, before the final exec line
such as:

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=(path to Rlib.so should be part of this)
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=...
...

I like Saptarshi's suggestion of moving R to the nodes for every job.
We have this setup by default on our institutional cluster since all
nodes can see my home directory, and it makes things really nice.

> > exec R CMD _path_to_imperious.so_ --slave --silent --vanilla --max-

HBase is there. But in order to use HBase as inputformat, it is best to write ones own HBaseInputFormat
and it include the JAR file using rhmr(,...jar=)

the tricky thing is hbase keys and values are raw bytes. So it can be passed over to RHIPE but how does
on intelligently specify the rowkeys (as raw bytes in RHIPE)?.

>

> > exec R CMD _path_to_imperious.so_ --slave --silent --vanilla --max-

>
> > rhoptions(runner="_path_to_Rsetup.sh_")
